title: Ops roadmap telemetry snapback
content:
Working notes / sketch for a lightweight operational roadmap + telemetry + snapback checklist. Purpose: create a single-page, pragmatic tracker that ties roadmap milestones to observable KPIs and clear snapback (rollback/fallback) triggers so engineers + ops know exactly when and how to step in during a roll forward.

Context and why this exists:
- Product-ops observed ambiguity during the last Dedicated rollout: multiple alerts fired but owners disagreed on severity and the rollback timing. We need a concise mapping: milestone -> critical telemetry -> action.
- This doc is intentionally terse, designed to be pasted into a briefing and linked to dashboards.

High-level structure (intended UX)
1) Milestone header (one line)
2) Critical KPIs (3–5 metrics) with thresholds and directionality
3) Primary + secondary owners and responders (with Slack handle)
4) Observable dashboards / panels and short link (dashboard id)
5) Snapback decision rule (binary yes/no with steps)
6) Post-action notes / mitigation checklist

Example entry (canonical format)
- Milestone: Hosted API v2.1 model switch (gradual canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%)
- Window: 2025-03-10 09:00 -> 2025-03-12 18:00 PT
- KPIs (primary):
  - p95 request latency (text/generation paths) — threshold: > 350ms for 10m continuous => ACTION A
  - error rate (HTTP 5xx + inference internal errors) — threshold: > 0.75% sustained for 5m => ACTION A
  - token cost per 1k avg (billing probe) — threshold: +20% vs baseline 7d median => ACTION B (investigate but don't block)
  - model quality regressions (eval metric: semantic-sim delta) — threshold: > 3.0 absolute drop on evaluation set => immediate stop and rollback
- Owners: Priya Nair (product-ops, @priya), Ethan Park (serving-runtime lead, @ethan), Maya Rodriguez (SRE, @maya)
- Dashboards: Hosted-api/model-switch/p95-panel (dash-1223), errors/5xx-summary (dash-900), cost/token-compare (dash-314)
- Snapback rule: If ACTION A metric fires twice within a 30m window OR model-quality threshold crossed once => execute Snapback Plan A (canary rollback to previous model build, scale down new traffic to 0, open incident channel).
- Snapback Plan A steps (ordered):
  1) Pause new canary increments via rollout controller (ethan)
  2) Re-route traffic to previous model variant (infra toggle /maya)
  3) Notify affected internal partners (ops-email + #prodops-alerts) and update status page (priya)
  4) Start triage doc: link to JIRA POPS-4310 and create postmortem stub (samir)
  5) If rollback fails or errors spike during rollback, escalate to SRE on-call and consider capacity fallback (use Dedicated reserve pool).

Readiness signals (pre-launch checklist) — quick pass/fail items:
- Canary smoke passes (synthetic probes) — runbook: synthetic-runner/hosted-api/v2/smoke (pass >= 98% of probes)
- Autoscaling baseline validated at expected qps (load test) — pass: 95th latency under target at forecast peak
- Cost guardrails configured (token cap + alert) — pass: budget cap set with soft throttles at 80%
- Telemetry hooks present in canary path: tracing, kv-cache hit ratio, token-metering — pass: each hook returns data within first 10m of canary
- Rollout playbook reviewed and owners confirmed in Slack thread #rollouts (emoji +1 from each owner)

KPI tracker template (single line entries; copy into sheet/dash)
- ID | Milestone | Window | KPI:metric | Threshold | Owner | DashPanel | SnapbackAction | Notes
- eg: R-132 | model-switch-v2.1 | 2025-03-10..12 | p95-latency | >350ms/10m | @ethan | dash-1223 | SnapbackA | baseline 7d median 260ms

Common telemetry signals and tuned thresholds (suggested defaults)
- Latency p50 / p95 / p99 (text gen): p95 threshold = baseline*1.35 or absolute 350ms (whichever tighter)
- Error rate (5xx): threshold 0.5% for non-critical windows, 0.75% for canary/rollout windows
- Model quality eval delta: >2.0 absolute drop on curated eval set -> fail
- KV/cache hit ratio: drop >15% vs baseline -> indicative of cold-cache regressions
- Token cost per 1k: +25% over 7d median triggers cost review; +40% triggers immediate pause for non-PII tests

Communication and incident channels
- Incident channel: #prodops-rollouts (open immediately when snapback action triggered)
- Pager escalation: SRE on-call -> infra lead -> eng manager (mech in PagerDuty roster)
- Status updates cadence: 1) immediate action note in channel; 2) 15m cadence until stable; 3) summary log at end of window

Post-action (post snapback) checklist
- Triage doc created and initial hypotheses listed (owner: samir)
- CI artifacts saved: model build id, canary request samples, traces, kv-cache snapshots, tokens used report
- Run a reduced-scope replay against previous model to verify if regression is model-specific or infra-related
- Decide whether to reattempt rollout (with narrower traffic increments, extra probes) or to freeze milestone and schedule rollback postmortem

Operational notes / heuristics (notes to self)
- Prefer binary snapback rules (simple, actionable) rather than probabilistic thresholds for on-call decisions.
- Label dashboards with roadmap milestone id (R-###) to make filtering during incidents trivial.
- When in doubt, prioritize availability and predictable latency for user-facing paths; cost anomalies are important but secondary during major launches.
- Keep an explicit callout for quality regressions — they should trump cost if user-facing correctness is impacted.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Do we want a lightweight UI in Console that maps active rollouts to these snapback rules? (MVP: a CSV import to the rollout controller)
- How to standardize the eval set per product vertical so model-quality thresholds are comparable? (prod + applied-ml engineering)
- Should we add a cost-auto-throttle for expensive embedding jobs during rollouts? (finance + infra)

Immediate next steps (this doc owner)
- Turn canonical format above into a one-row sheet template and share with product-ops for next sprint (due 2025-03-07) — Priya
- Create dashboard quick-links and tag them with R-ids (dash owners: Maya + Ethan)
- Pilot the format on next small canary (R-132) and gather feedback in retrospective

Scratch / raw notes (keep at bottom):
- 2025-02-26 — noticed cost spike in experiment X when kv cache warmed; might need warmup stage before rolling new quantized variant.
- PRs to watch: repo/infra#812 (rollout-controller: safe pause API), repo/serving#997 (kv-cache improvements).
- Linked ticket: POPS-4310 (canary rollback postmortem)

End of working draft.

(If this becomes useful, will convert into a Confluence brief and a light CSV template for import.)
